OBITUARY REFERENCE 
MR. CHAIRMAN: Hon. Members, I refer with profound sorrow to the assing 
awary of Shri M. Falaniyandi, a former member of this House on le 8th March, 
2005 at the age of 87 years. 
Born at Tiruchirapally, Tamil Nadu in December, 1918, Shri Palaniyandi ad his 
education at E.R. High School, Tiruchirapally. A social worker and trade unionist, 
Shri Palaniyandi took special interest in the welfare of owntr odden sections of 
the society and took part in various trade union activities and Kisan movements. 
He was also the President of the Tamil nadu National Cement Workers' Federation 
and Tamil Nadu National Sugar Workers' Federation. 
The distinguished legislative career of Shri Palaniyandi started with the 
membership of the erstwhile Madras Legislative Assembly, from 1952 to 957. 
He was also elected to the Second Lok Sabha. Shri Palaniyandi presented the 
State of Tamil Nadu in this House from June, 1986 to June, 1992. 
 In the passing away of Shri M. Palaniya ndi, the country has lost a ited social 
worker, and an active trade union leader. We deeply mourn  passing away of 
Shri M. Palaniyandi. 
I request Members to rise in their places and observe silence as a mark respect to 
the memory of the departed. 
(Hon. Members then stood in silence for one minute)

TRIBUTES TO MARTYRS BHAGAT SINGH,  
RAJ GURU AND SUKHDEV 
MR. CHAIRMAN: Hon. Members, as you are aware, today is the anniversary 
of the martyrdom of the revolutionaries Bhagat Singh, Raj Guru and Sukhdev 
who laid down their lives at the gallows on this day in 1931. Their self-sacrifice 
has made all of us proud. The nation can never forget them. 
Hon. Members, let us pay our homage to all those great souls whose 
supreme sacrifice led to India's independence. We pledge ourselves to uphold 
the cherished values for which they laid down their lives. 
I would now request Members to rise in their places and observe silence, as 
a mark of respect in memory of the martyrs.

Undertrials in Jails 
*301. SHRI RAM NATH KOVIND:  
 SHRIS.S.AHLUWALIA:† 
Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that a large number of accused in custody are 
awaiting investigations/trials; 
(b) the details of persons held in custody in jails pending investigations/ trials 
as on 1st January, 2005 with break-up of periods in custody; 
(c) the number of those detained vide Police Challans and vide Complaints 
to Magistrates; 
(d) the proportions of acquittals by trials in cases initiated vide Police 
Challans and those vide Complaints to Magistrates; 
(e) whether any review has been undertaken especially with a view to 
ascertain the rationale between the rate of complaints and convictions; and 
(f) if so, the findings thereof? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS 
(SHRI MANIKRAO HODLYA GAVIT): (a) to (f) A Statement is laid on the 
Table of the House. 
Statement 
Undertrials in Jails 
'Police' and 'Public Order are State subjects as per the Seventh Schedule to the 
Constitution of India. The detection, re gistration, investigation, prosecution 
and prevention of crimes, is the responsibility of the State Governments. As 
per the statistics available with the National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB), 
the number of undertrials held in prison at the end of 2003 was 217659. Their 
break up as per the periods of custody in prison is as follows: 
Upto three months                                  91956 
Three months to one year                    85966 
More than one year                                   39732 
Total                                                                              217659 
 
†The question was actually asked on the floor of the House by SHRI 
S.S.AHLUWALIA

RAJYA SABHA [23 March, 2005] 
No specific review has been undertaken  to ascertain the rationale between 
the rate of complaints and convictions. However, the Government of India had set 
up a Committee under Justice V.S. Malimath to consider and recommend 
measures for revamping the Criminal Justice System. The Committee on 
Reforms of the Criminal Justice System observed that prompt and quality 
investigation is the foundation of effective criminal justice system. The Committee 
made certain recommendations to make the institution of criminal 
investigation and prosecution synergetic with other institutions and effective in 
delivering good results. Since 'Police' and 'Public Order' are State subjects, the 
recommendations were sent to the States for further process. 
It may be mentioned that the details of those detained vide police challans 
and vide complaints to Magistrates and the proportion of acquittals by trial in cases 
initiated vide police challans and those vide complaints to Magistrates are not 
maintained by the NCRB.

Statement 
(a) The National Electricity Policy has been notified on 12.2.2005. 
(b) Protecting the interest of consumers is one of the major aims of the 
Electricity Act, 2003. The main objectives of the National Electricity 
Policy are mentioned below:— 
* Access to Electricity—Available for all households in next five 
years. 
. * Availability of Power—Demand to be fully met by 2012. Energy and 
peaking shortages to be overcome and 5 per cent spinning reserve to 
be available. 
* Supply of Reliable and Quality Power of Specified standards in an 
efficient manner and at reasonable rates. 
* Per capita availability of electricity to be increased to over 1000 units 
by 2012. 
* Minimun lifeline consumption of 1 unit/household/day as a merit good 
by year 2012. 
* Financial Turnaround and Commercial Viability of Electricity 
Sector. 
* Protection of consumers' interests.

Governments in accordance with the provi sions of the Act. Suggestions and

envisages the following:— 
* Consumers, particularly those who are ready to pay a tariff which 
reflects efficient costs, have the right to get uninterrupted twenty four 
hours supply of quality power. 
* Regulatory Commission to specify standards of performance by 
utilities. 
* Reliability Index (Rl) of supply of power to consumers to be 
indicated by distribution licensees and road map for declaration of Rl 
for all cities and towns up to the District Headquarter towns as 
also for rural areas, to be draw n up by SERCs. Rl data to be 
compiled and published by CEA.

up of grievance redressal forum by the licensees within 6 months.

regarding Ombudsman and also appoint/designate the 
Ombudsman within six months. The Ombudsman shall look into 
non-redressal of consumer grievances by the forum. 
* Central Government, State Governments and Regulatory 
Commissions to facilitate capacity building of consumer groups and 
their effective representation before the Regulatory Commissions 
for enhancing the efficacy of regulatory process. 
* State Governments to prepare Fi ve Year Plan with annual 
milestones to bring down transmission and distribution losses 
expeditiously. Central Government would provide incentive based 
assistance to States that are ab le to reduce losses as per agreed 
programmes. 
* Multi-Year Tariff framework to minimize risks for utilities and 
consumers, promote efficiency and rapid reduction of system losses. 
This would also bring greater predictability to consumer tariffs by 
restricting tariff adjustments to known indicators such as power 
purchase prices and inflation indices. 
* For thermal power, economics of generation and supply of 
electricity to be the basis for choice of fuel from among the 
options available.

efficiency of operations in all the segm ents of the industry and for evolving 
suitable performance norms of operations together with incentives and

Origin of the civil defence initiatives in the country 
*320. SHRI S.S. AHLUWALIA: Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS 
be pleased to state: 
(a) whether, besides Police system in the States/UTs, there are other auxiliary 
localized institutions e.g.  Resistance Group, Volunteer Force, etc., promoted 
by citizens' initiatives for maintenance of social/communal harmony etc.; 
(b) when were such auxiliary units introduced in our system and their details 
as of now; 
(c) the details of the Civil Defence initiatives in the country; 
(d) the details of Government supports to such initiatives, including 
revisions, if any, effected from time to time, since Independence; 
(e) when was the module of training in Civil Defence formulated; and 
(f) the details of revisions, if any carried out therein so far? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS 
(SHRI S. REGUPATHY): (a) and (b) In In dia, Home Guards were raised in 
Bomaby in December 1946, to assi st the police in controlling Civil 
disturbances and communal riots. Subsequently, this concept of a voluntary 
citizens force, as an auxiliary to the Police for maintenance of law and order 
and for meeting emergencies like floods, fires, famines, etc. was adopted by 
several others States such as Paranti Raksha Dal, West Bengal Village block 
and Civic Guards. After 1962, the Centre advised the States and Union 
Territories to merge their existing voluntary organizations into one All India 
Force known as 'Home Guards' which would be voluntary both in concept and 
character. Home guards provide support to the State administration in hours of 
need including maintenance of social and communal harmony. 
(c)'and (d) The policy of the Government of India till 1962 was confined to 
making the States and Union Territories conscious of the need of Civil Defence 
measures and to ask them to keep r eady Civil Defence Paper Plans for major 
cities and towns. Two major events which gave a filling to formalization of 
Civil Defence set-up in India, since independence were to two wars in 1960s'. 
The Civil Defence was given legal status by the Civil Defence Act passed by 
Parliament in 1968. The Government 
45 

RAJYA SABHA [23 March, 2005] 
supports the civil defence set-up in the country by providing logistic and 
financial support to the states for raising, training and equipping them from 
time to time. 
(e) and (f) Civil defence training was introduced after 1962. There has been 
constant review & upgradation of training module from time to time keeping in 
view the requirements in the changing scenario.

Production of medicines patented abroad 
2334. SHRI UDAY PRATAP SINGH: Will the Minister of COMMERCE 
AND INDUSTRY be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that a number of  medicines are available in India 
which are patented abroad and their patents are still valid; 
(b) what will be the status of these medicines under the new Patent Law; 
and 
(c) whether the Indian companies will be required to stop the pr oduction 
of these medicines which are already being manufactured by them? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE AND 
INDUSTRY (SHRI E.V.K.S. ELANGOVAN): (a) to (c) Patents are granted under 
the sovereign prerogative of countries according to their respective Patent Laws 
and only have territorial effect. Accordingly, the availability of medicines in 
India, which are patented abroad, is not affected unless a patent for the same 
exists in India. As per the new patent regime introduced through the Patents 
(Amendment) Ordinance, 2004, effective from 1st January, 2005, patent rights 
to applications for medicines or drugs filed under Section 5(2) of the Patents 
Act shall accrue only from the date of grant of patent in India. Thus, the Indian 
manufacturers can continue to manufacture such drugs for which patent 
protection is not valid in India.

Unified command to tackle naxal menace 
2370. DR. MAM. RAMASWAMY:  
SHRI C. RAMACHANDRAIAH: 
Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS be pleased to refer to Unstarred 
Question 2126 given in the Rajya Sabha on 22nd December, 2004 and state: 
(a) the details of States which have opposed unified command to fight 
naxal/terrorism in the country; 
(b) the reasons given by the States in this regard; and 
(c) the other measures being taken by Union Government for socio-
economic development of concerned distri cts of naxal affected States in the 
country? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS 
(SHRI SRIPRAKASH JAISWAL): (a) and (b) There is no proposal, at 
present, to setup a unified command to fight naxalism. 
(c) Keeping in view that the naxal problem is not merely a law and order 
problem, the Central Government has adopted a multi-pronged counter strategy 
which takes into account the security as well as development aspects of the 
problem. 
The Government has asked the naxal affected States to intensify anti-naxalite 
operations keeping the door for a peace dialogue with naxal groups open. Besides 
reviewing and co-ordinating the steps teken by the States to counter the menace 
of naxalism by the Coordination Centre and the Task Force on Naxalism, the 
MHA provides financial assistance to the naxal affected States in the form of 
reimbursement of the security related expenditure under the Security Related 
Expenditure (SRE) scheme. Funds are also provided for modernization of State 
police forces for upgrading the weaponry, equipment mobility, training etc. under 
the Police Modernization (PM) scheme to enable them to effectively meet the 
threat to internal security and law and order posed by the naxals. 
104 

[23 March, 2005] RAJYA SABHA 
On the development side, the Central Government has advised the States to accord 
a higher priority in their annual plans for the accelerated integrated development of 
the naxal affected districts. On its part, the Central Government has included 55 
districts in 9 States badly affected by naxalism under the Backward Districts

AFFAIRS be pleased to state:

involved in online lotteries and hence it requires restriction;

lotteries illegal? 
105 

RAJYA SABHA [23 March, 2005] 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS 
(SHRI MANIKRAO HODLYA GAVIT): (a) to (d) The Lotteries (Regulation)

THE MINISTER OF POWER (SHRI P.M. SAYEED): (a) and (b) The 
electricity generation as well as power supply position in the country 
including that of Northern Region is reviewed on regular basis. In view of 
various initiatives taken by the Government, energy shortage in the country has 
declined from 8.8% in 2002-03 to 7.1 % in 2003-04 and 6.8% in 2004-05 till

Power shortages in the country including Northern Region are due to the 
growth in generation capacity addition not keeping pace with the growth in demand.

stations under various utilities in the Northern Region has been less than the

particularly in the catchment region of Bhakra reservoir.

of power stations in the country which have not generated as per their targets during

areas of the hydro reservoirs. This year, hydro generation has been low in the Northern

Low generation from thermal stations has been mainly due to: 
(i) Shortage of coal. 
(ii) Shortage of gas.

resources necessary for undertaking renovation, modernization and life extension 
schemes for old and inefficient generating units.

Increasing the per capita availability of power  
2420. DR. VIJAY MALLYA: 
SHRI LALIT SURI:  
Will the Minister of POWER be pleased to state: 
(a) whether a decision has been taken by Government to increase per capita availability 
of power over 1000 Units as against present availability -of 500 units; 
(b) what is the requirement of funds to achieve this target; 
(c) how the funds for the purpose are proposed to be raised; and 
(d) what are the other salient features of the policy and the details thereof? 
THE MINISTER OF POWER (SHRI P.M. SAYEED): (a) Yes Sir. The National 
Electricity Policy notified on 12th February, 2005 under the provisions of Section 3 of 
the Electricity Act, 2003, envisages increase of per capita availability of power to over 1000 
units by 2012. 
(b) To meet the objective of rapid economic growth and "power for all" 
161 

RAJYA SABHA [23 March, 2005] 
including completion of household electrification, the need for investment of about Rs. 
9,00,000 crores in generation, transmission, sub-transmission, distribution and rural 
electrification had been estimated in the 10th and 11th Plan periods. 
(c) Public sector investments, both at the Central Government and State Governments, has 
been envisaged and the need for attracting substantial private investment has been 
highlighted. 
(d) Salient features of the policy are given in the enclosed Statement. 
Statement 
Salient features of the National Electricity Policy 
1. Aims at accelerated development of power sector, providing supply of electricity to 
all areas and protecting interests of consumers and other stakeholders. 
2. Objectives: 
* Access to Electricity—Available for all households in next five 
years. 
* I Availability of Power—Demand to be fully met by 2012. Energy 
and peaking shortages to be overcome and spinning reserve to be available. 
* Supply of Reliable and Quality Power of specified standards in an efficient 
manner and at reasonable rates. 
* Per capita availability of electricity to be increased to over 1000 units by 
2012. 
* Minimum lifeline consumption of 1 unit/household/day as a merit good 
by year 2012. 
* Financial Turnaround and Commercial Viability of electricity Sector. 
* Protection of consumers' interests. 
 
3. CEA to notify first National Electricity Plan in six months with a perspective 
up 12th Plan period. The Plan prepared by CEA to be used by prospective 
generating companies, transmission utilities and transmission/distribution 
licensees as reference document. 
4. Development of Rural Electrification Distribution backbone, village electrification 
and household electrification to achieve the NCMP 
162 

[23 March, 2005] RAJYA SABHA 
target of completing household electrification in next five years. 
Financial support in terms of capital subsidy to States for rural 
electrification. Special preference to Dalit Bastis, Tribal Areas and other 
weaker sections for rural electrification. REC to be nodal agency for 
rural electrification at Central Government level. 
5. Creation of adequate generation capacity with a spinning reserve of at least 
5% by 2012 with availability of installed capacity at 85%. 
6. Full development of hydro potential. Provision of long tenor finance for 
these projects. 
7. Choice of fuel for thermal generation to be based on economics of 
generation and supply of electricity. 
8. Development of National Grid. 
9. Cost of recovery of service from consumers at tariff reflecting efficient costs 
to ensure financial viability of the sector 
 
10. Provision of support to lifeline consumers (households below poverty line 
having consumption of 3d units per month) in terms of tariffs. 
11. Availability Based Tariff (ABT) to be extended to State level for better grid 
discipline through economic signaling. 
 
12. Special emphasis on time bound reduction of transmission and 
distribution losses.  
13. Measures to promote competition aimed at consumer benefits. 
14. Reliability and quality of power supply to be monitored by State 
Elecetricity Regulatory Commissions. 
15. Exploitation of non-conventional energy sources such as small hydro, 
solar, biomass and wind for additional power generation capacity. 
Other Features 
16. Emphasis on achieving higher efficiency levels of generating plants 
through necessary renovation and modernization. 
17. Central Government to facilitate the continued development of 
national grid. CTU and STU to undertake coordinated planning and 
development. 
18. Transmission capacity to have redundancy level and margins as per 
international standards. 
163 

RAJYA SABHA [23 March, 2005] 
 
 per international standards. 
19. Adequate transitional financial support for reforming power utilities. 
Encouragement for private sector participation in distribution. 
20. The State Regulatory Commissions to put in place independent third party 
meter testing arrangement. 
21. Support for adoption of IT system for ensuring correct billing to consumers. 
22. Speedy implementation of stringent measures against theft of electricity. 
23. Full emphasis on augmentation of R&D base. Mission approach for identified 
priorities areas. 
24. Demand side management through energy conservation measures. Labels regarding 
energy efficiency to be displayed on appliances. Efficient agricultural pumpsets 
and efficient lighting technologies to be promoted. Appropraite tariff structure for 
managing the peak load. 
25. Special attention for developing training infrastructure in the field of regulation; 
trading and power market. 
26. For giving boost to renewable and non-conventional energy sources, a prescribed 
percentage of power, as pecified by State Regulatory Commissions, to be 
purchased from such sources of energy at the earliest 
27. Necessary regulations and appointing Ombudsman for redressal of consumers' 
grievances to be in place in six months. 
Electrification of one lakh villages and one crore households 
2421. SHRI ANAND SHARMA: Will the Minister of POWER be pleased to state: 
(a) what are the annual targets of Government's programme of 
electrification of one lakh villages and one crore households by the year 
2012 and the year-wise financial outlay for this purpose; and 
(b) the names of the agencies implementing the scheme, their obligations 
and means to achieve the target? 
THE MINISTER OF POWER (SHRI P.M. SAYEED): (a) and (b) Anew scheme of 
rural electricity Infrastructure and Household Electrification has 
164 

[23 March, 2005] RAJYA SABHA 
been approved for the attainment of the National Common Minimum Programme of 
completing Rural Household Electrification in five years by replacing the earlier 40% 
Capital Subsidy Scheme. Under this scheme 90% Capital Subsidy would be 
provided for: 
(i) Creation of Rural Electricity Distribution Backbone (REDB) with one 33/11 
Kv (or 66/11 kV) substation in every block appropriately linked to the State 
Transmission System. 
(ii) Creation of Village Electricity Infrastructure (VEI) for electrification of all un-
electrified villages/habitations with distribution transformer(s) in 
every village/habitation. 
(iii) Decentralized Distributed Generation (DDG) and Supply System for 
Villages/Habitations where grid supply is not cost effective and where 
Ministry of Non-Conventional energy Sources would not be providing 
electricity through their programme(s). 
(iv) Electrification of all un-elect rified Below Poverty Line (BPL) 
households in the country free of charge. 
The estimated expenditure for 1st phase of the Scheme is Rs. 5000 crore for the 
remaining period of 10th Plan. 
The scheme would be implemented through the Rural Electrification Corporation 
(REC), a Public Sector Undertaking under this Ministry. The services of Central Public 
Sector Undertakings have been offered to States who would like to use them for execution 
of projects under this scheme and the modalities have been worked out in the 
Memorandum of Understanding that REC has entered into with NTPC, POWERGRID, 
NHPC and DVC to make available CPSUs' project management expertise and 
capabilities to States wishing to use their services.

Guidelines for power purchasing policy 
2427. SHRI SUDARSHAN AKARAPU: Will the Minister of POWER be

process of distribution licenses including the price at which electricity shall be procured

years.

the shortages prevailing in different regions/States, transfer of power from

Crisis of potable water in Rajasthan 
†2447. DR. PRABHA THAKUR: Will the Minister of RURAL 
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Rajasthan falls in the category of States facing severe crisis of 
potable water; 
(b) whether there is acute shortage of potable water and many districts of the 
State are facing the crisis of contaminated potable water which has fluoride 
contents; 
(c) whether Central Government plans to provide special economic grants to 
Rajasthan for providing pure potable water to the public of Rajasthan under 
National Water Policy granting special status to Rajasthan keeping in view the 
potable water crisis there; and

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL 
DEVELOPMENT (SHRI A. NARENDRA): (a) and (b) Some of the State 
Governments, including Rajasthan, report crisis of potable water, especially during 
summer months. As per the Comprehensive Action Plan prepared in 1999 to 
cover all the rural habitations in the country with safe drinking water supply, and 
the subsequent coverage reported by the State, there are 91,161 fully covered, 
2785 not covered habitations in the State. The 
†Original notice of the question was received in Hindi. 
190 

[23 March, 2005] RAJYA SABHA 
State has completed a fresh habitation survey to ascertain the latest status of 
drinking water supply in rural habitations, including the freshly emerged 
habitations and those slipped back from their earlier fully covered status. These 
results are yet to be validated by an independent agency. As per the Water 
Quality Survey ordered in March, 2000, the State Government has reported 
41,072 rural habitations having chemical quality problems, out of which 8992 
habitations are affected with excess fluoride. 
(c) and (d) Rural drinking water supply  is a State subject. Government of 
India provides financial and technical assistance to States to accelerate coverage 
of rural habitations through a Centrally Sponsored Scheme, namely 
Accelerated Rural Water Supply Programme (ARWSP). 
The inter-State allocation criterion for ARWSP funds provide for 40% 
weightage for rural population, 35% for hydrological conditions, 15% for 
NC/PC villages and 10% for quality affected villages. The State Government can 
utilize 15% of the ARWSP annual allocation for tackling quality problems. 
5% of ARWSP funds are ear-marked for rural water supply in DDP areas and 
Rajasthan get funds in proportion to the number of NSS habitation without safe 
sources. 
Apart from these, 5% of total ARWSP funds are released for meeting 
contingencies arising out of natural cal amities and emergent situations like 
drought etc. 
Thus, the hydrological conditions in Rajasthan are duly reflected in the 
proportionate annual allocation of funds to the State.

2456. SHRI JANARDHAN A POOJARY: Will the Minister of RURAL 
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that a number of NGOs are blacklisted for 
misappropriation of funds extended for undertaking various rural development 
programmes; 
(b) if so, what are the details, within quantum of funds sanctioned and 
accounted for during the last three years, year-wise and State-wise; 
(c) whether any inquiry has been initiated for fixing responsibility for 
indiscreet sanctions and action taken against defaulting NGOs and for 
recovery of the sanctioned amount; and 
(d) if so, the details in this regard? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL 
DEVELOPMENT (SHRIMATI SURYAKANTA PATIL): (a) Yes, Sir. 
(b) The names and addresses of the organizations blacklisted, amount 
sanctioned and released, State-wise and year-wise during the last three years, are 
given in the enclosed Statement (see below). 
(c) Yes, Sir. The projects sanctioned to the NGOs are periodically 
monitored to ensure percolation of bene fits to the intended beneficiaries and 
proper utilization of grant in aid released to them. Defaulting NGOs are given 
opportunities to rectify mistakes committed, failing which, such NGOs are 
blacklisted. FIRs are filed against them for recovery of misutilised funds. 
(d) During the last three years, CAPART has blacklisted 66 NGOs for 
committing various irregularities, out of which 35 NGOs have been 
blacklisted during the year 2004-05 only (till 15th March, 2005) for 
submitting forged documents. 30 out of 35 NGOs have not received any fund 
from CAPART. FIRs have been filed against erring organisations and its 
functionaries at the concerned Police Stations.

As per the report of NCW the problems faced by Women Carpet Weavers include: 
lack of social security; lack of awareness of Government schemes; exploitation by 
private traders; no schools for girls near their Villages beyond class-V; lack of 
drinking water and health facilities. 
The State Government of Uttar Pradesh has been requested to take steps to 
solve the problems related to drinking water, health etc. The Carpet Export 
Promotion Council (CEPC) and All India Carpet Manufacturing Association, 
Bhadohi have bee advised to ensure compliance as per law provisions.

Plan and separate Marine Police Wing 
SHRI LEKHRAJ BACHANI (Gujarat): Sir, Gujarat has a coastal line of 1640 
kms. In order to provide adequate secu rity for the coastal areas, a Coastal 
Security Plan for Rs.392 crores was submitted to the Government of India. 
We suggest that the Navy and Coast Guard should be made solely 
responsible for patrolling of the high seas and the coastal security of the territorial 
waters of Gujarat. Though it is a fact that the prime responsibility of ensuring 
complete maritime security lies with the Indian Coast Guard, which cannot be 
ignored or diluted, the pr esent proposal incorporat es the role of State 
Police,however, limited in nature, which can only be as supplementary 
assistance to the existing coastal security. There are a number of creeks and 
uninhabited islands, very close to Gujarat, towards Pakistan side. These creeks 
and islands may become a safe haven for infiltrators, smugglers etc. for anti-
national activities. It is, therefore, requested that the Government of India should 
make appropriate addition to the present coastal security set up of Navy and the 
Coast Guard, and also consider setting up of separate marine police wing in 
each coastal police station, which should be properly equipped and trained.

SHRI R.K. ANAND (Jharkhand): Sir, it is really awesome that even after more 
than five decades of our Independence, diseases like TB and Malaria are spreading

die of TB every year in the country. Today Malaria cases are around 2 to 3 million

Most of the inhabitants are tribals and workers of various mines, mainly coal 
mines. Due to poverty leading to malnutrition has resulted in rising TB cases in 
the State. During 2000 to September, 2002, as many as 178 TB patients died due

Malaria. Cases of other vector-borne diseases like Dengue, Kala Azar and Japanese 
Encephalitis and Filariasis are also ra mpant. The Government on its parts is 
implementing DOTS as WHO recommended strategy to control TB but coverage 
has to be rapidly increased in the State. Central assistance is needed for 
establishing more and more diagnostic centres in the State so that TB cases are 
diagnosed well in time to start right treatment under DOTS. 
Malaria is a local and focal problem in the State. It turns epidemic during the 
summer and rainy seasons. To reduce the malaria cases, mosquitoes need to 
be eliminated. Diagnostic centres need to be incresed. The people in tribal and 
village areas need to be supplied with adequate supplies of approved 
insecticides and larvicides, medicated bed nets for personal protection apart from 
adequate quantities of anti-malaria drugs through village level health centres. In 
this, village panchayats can also be involved. Information campaigns also needed 
to be launched.
